transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood Solutions), Priya Kapoor (Head of ML, MercuryTrust), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Derek Shaw (CTO), Anita Rao (Security)

--- Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect) ---
Samantha: Quick scope of POC -> workload modeling, QPS, concurrency, token distributions, success criteria.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samantha Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this focused on the workload characterization side of the POC, get a clear success criteria and then plan the bench runs. uhm, can we do a quick round of intros?
[00:12] Priya Kapoor: yeah hi, i'm priya, head of ml at mercurytrust, we own the models and the product integrations.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: liam, platform eng, i'll handle infra and logs.
[00:21] Derek Shaw: derek, cto, dropping in for high level timeline and risk.
[00:24] Anita Rao: anita, security — I'll validate compliance needs.
[00:26] Carlos Mendes: carlos, se at redwood, i'll lead the benchmarking and performance tuning.
[00:29] Jordan Kim: jordan — solutions, will support rollouts and runbooks.
[00:32] Samantha Lee: great. quick agenda: 1) current production traffic / patterns 2) target success criteria for POC 3) concrete metrics we need to collect (qps, concurrency, token histograms) 4) bench plan and timelines. sound good?
[00:40] Priya Kapoor: sounds good. first question — we have two main flows: chat-assisted support (interactive) and nightly batch summarization. chat is low-middle QPS but very latency sensitive; batch is high token volume, tolerant of higher latency.
[00:56] Carlos Mendes: ok that's a very common split. do you have rough numbers for qps and concurrency per region?
[01:03] Liam O'Connor: we can give ballparks — chat peaks at about 25 qps globally, sustained around 8 qps during business hours. concurrency per chat session is usually 1-2 active requests but bursts hit up to about 60 concurrent requests in a region during campaigns. batch: we submit nightly jobs that create about 25M input tokens across the job and we typically run 6 parallel workers for that batch.
[01:29] Samantha Lee: perfect — that's the kind of detail we need. for the POC scope we usually size for peak chat qps plus a representative batch run; we also need token distribution (input prompt lengths and generated output lengths). can you share sample histograms?
[01:44] Priya Kapoor: we have logs but need to massage them — prompts vary a lot, 50% of chat prompts are under 120 tokens, 30% 120-400, tail to ~1200. outputs are usually shorter, median ~80 tokens, p95 ~350 tokens. batch prompts are longer — median 800 tokens in, with outputs ~1200 tokens.
[02:05] Derek Shaw: target success criteria from our side — for interactive chat p95 latency should be under 300ms if possible, overall infra cost for POC should not exceed $2,500 for the pilot run, and batch should finish within our nightly window (3 hours). those are, like, top-level.
[02:26] Jordan Kim: quick clarification — 300ms p95 is tight depending on model size and quantization; do you have a preferred model family or are you flexible?
[02:33] Priya Kapoor: we want commercially reasonable quality; leaning toward an efficient open model (redwood-curated or similar) — quality tests will be part of the eval. we're flexible if the latency/cost tradeoff is clear.
[02:45] Carlos Mendes: ok so for the POC we'll propose two model variants: 1) latency-optimized (quantized 8-bit with lower context) for chat; 2) high-throughput medium-quality variant for batch. in the bench we'll run both and show cost/latency curves.
[03:00] Liam O'Connor: what about concurrency and batching — we do have session affinity so chat sessions often reuse KV caches for multi-turn. will that be part of the bench?
[03:10] Carlos Mendes: yes, good point. we need to emulate KV cache warm and cold scenarios. we'll run microbenchmarks to show with warmed cache (prefix reuse) vs cold starts. that has a big effect on latency and tokens per call.
[03:23] Samantha Lee: great — let's enumerate the exact telemetry we'll collect during the POC: qps, concurrent active requests, p50/p95/p99 latency, input token histogram, output token histogram, tokens per second, GPU utilization, and cost estimate per million tokens. any other?
[03:39] Anita Rao: audit logs and encryption at rest — we need to confirm logs retention policy and whether the POC can use customer-managed KMS in the private deployment.
[03:48] Jordan Kim: we can support KMS for Private. for Hosted we'll provide audit logs and limited retention; we'll document differences in the runbook.
[03:55] Priya Kapoor: ok that's fine. on sample data — we'll strip PII and share anonymized logs. do you need the full request/response or just metadata plus token counts?
[04:04] Carlos Mendes: ideally both: a small sample of full requests to validate prompt shapes and a larger csv of metadata (timestamps, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency, route). that'll let us build the token histograms and simulate the exact distribution.
[04:18] Samantha Lee: timeline check — today is Mar 4. our proposed timeline: get logs and sizing template this week (by Mar 10), redwood prepares harness and sizing within the same week, run benchmark week of Mar 16, deliver findings and cost model week of Mar 23, then iterate. ok?
[04:35] Derek Shaw: that timeline sounds doable but we need to see the bandwidth cost of logs export — liam will confirm.
[04:40] Liam O'Connor: i'll check and flag any blockers.
[04:42] Priya Kapoor: success criteria — to formalize: 1) interactive chat p95 <= 300ms (or show plan to reach this within 2 weeks of tuning), 2) batch completes within 3 hours and cost per 1M tokens < $X (we'll accept redwood's estimate), 3) no security blockers for hosted/priv deploy per anita.
[05:04] Carlos Mendes: note on the 300ms — that'll depend on model size and whether warm cache is expected. for example, with a warmed KV cache and a 13B quantized model we can often hit ~200-350ms p95 on A100-equivalent infra; on smaller GPUs or on-hosted cheaper tiers the number shifts. we'll produce a latency vs cost chart.
[05:25] Samantha Lee: can we be more specific about qps profile? Priya mentioned peaks of ~25 qps globally — are peaks per region localized or global?
[05:33] Priya Kapoor: mostly global but about 60% of traffic is NA, 25% EU, 15% APAC. region-level peaks in NA hit 18 qps, sometimes 30 during campaigns.
[05:45] Carlos Mendes: that helps. for the bench we'll size for NA peak (30 qps) as worst case and also run scaled tests at 8 qps baseline.
[05:54] Liam O'Connor: for batch — 25M input tokens, split across 6 workers — can you estimate expected GPU time?
[06:01] Carlos Mendes: very rough: depends on model throughput (tokens/sec). e.g., a 7B quantized model might do 200-600 tokens/sec per GPU depending on batching; at 400 tokens/sec, 25M tokens is ~62.5k seconds of GPU time ~17.4 GPU-hours; split across 6 workers that's ~3 GPU-hours each plus overhead. we'll run calibrated bench to get accurate numbers.
[06:29] Samantha Lee: good. we'll include that back-of-envelope in the sizing doc.
[06:33] Priya Kapoor: about dataset privacy — for POC can we run on hosted or do you require private?
[06:39] Jordan Kim: hosted is fastest to start and we can do anonymized logs; if you need customer-managed KMS or VPC peering we recommend Redwood Private and we can scope that in parallel. for the POC most customers start hosted to iterate on prompts and perf, then move to Private for final runs.
[06:55] Anita Rao: security gating items: SOC2 evidence, SIEM integration points, KMS support, and data residency guarantees. we'll need the security pack and contacts.
[07:05] Samantha Lee: noted — we'll share the security artifacts and a short memo on hosted vs private compliance differences.
[07:10] Priya Kapoor: can we capture some specific benchmark scenarios? e.g., chat single-turn cold start, chat multi-turn warmed cache (3 turns), burst 60 concurrent connections, batch full run with 6 workers.
[07:21] Carlos Mendes: yes we'll define scenarios and test scripts. i'll enumerate them in the runbook: scenario A cold single-turn, B warmed multi-turn, C burst concurrency, D nightly batch.
[07:31] Liam O'Connor: also include a canary with traffic mirroring of 1% for live validation; do you support transparent mirroring?
[07:38] Jordan Kim: we can help set up a mirroring route or synthetic traffic generator. for POC we'll probably do synthetic replay from logs to avoid live production risk.
[07:47] Samantha Lee: pricing for POC — for hosted bench runs there is usually an eval credit or a small usage charge; for dedicated/private there will be quoting. we'll send an initial estimate.
[07:56] Priya Kapoor: for the cost success criteria — we'll accept Redwood's estimated $/1M tokens if you show assumptions and GPU pricing.
[08:05] Carlos Mendes: we'll include a cost model with assumptions: GPU SKU, billed GPU-hours, average tokens/sec, batching factor, cache hit rates.
[08:15] Derek Shaw: one risk — if model quality is insufficient we'll need to know fallback options and how long tuning might take.
[08:22] Samantha Lee: yes — part of the evaluation will be quality metrics: simple automated evals and a small human review of sample outputs. we'll capture those in the report.
[08:33] Priya Kapoor: timeline check again — when do you need sample logs?
[08:36] Samantha Lee: by Mar 10 we'll need the logs to stay on the proposed timeline.
[08:40] Priya Kapoor: ok we'll aim for that.
[08:43] Anita Rao: also include a security contact in the deck so we can triage early.
[08:47] Samantha Lee: will do.
[08:49] Carlos Mendes: technical note — when you export logs, include request_id, timestamp, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, latency_ms, route, and a small sample of raw prompts (anonymized). that allows us to build the token histograms and synth load driver.
[09:05] Liam O'Connor: will do.
[09:07] Samantha Lee: ok before we wrap — quick recap and concrete next steps.
[09:12] Samantha Lee: recap: 1) Customer to provide anonymized logs + top 50 prompt templates by Mar 10. 2) Redwood to send sizing template and initial cost model by Mar 6. 3) Redwood to prepare benchmark harness and v1 test scripts by Mar 9. 4) Benchmark run scheduled week of Mar 16; deliverable report week of Mar 23. security pack to be shared by Mar 6.
[09:36] Priya Kapoor: sounds good. one more — can you include memory footprint estimates per model variant? we need to ensure GPUs have enough memory for context windows.
[09:44] Carlos Mendes: yes we'll attach memory and GPU selection guidance in the sizing doc.
[09:49] Derek Shaw: ok thanks, appreciate the structured plan.
[09:52] Samantha Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and create the shared folder for logs.
[09:58] Priya Kapoor: thanks everyone.
[10:00] meeting end
